claim_a: The 1916 year belongs to Boeing Aircraft Company, a Washington corporation, which the reporting company merely owns
claim_b: Boeing was originally incorporated in Washington in 1916 and was reincorporated in Delaware in 1934
claim_b_source: S4526 registrant recital, S-4 and S-4/A
why_they_differ: One is the company describing its own formation eight months after the fact; the other is the same institution sixty-two years later compressing the chain into one person. A third in-window recital (S4517) calls the 1927 contract party a WASHINGTON corporation named Boeing Airplane Company, Incorporated.
evidence_weight: A and the federal recital are in-window Tier-1; B is retrospective and cannot witness a 1916 act. A is self-narrative, one lineage, two document years.
best_supported_interpretation: The bytes support: 1916 is a year a Boeing-named Washington manufacturing corporation was operating; 1934 is the year the reporting company began; and no held document says the two are one person. Write the origin as a split.
residual_uncertainty: Whether the 1934 holding took the older name while the operating company took the newer, or the reverse. Routes: Washington and Delaware charter records; family (e).
confidence: UNKNOWN (resolution) / High (that the conflict is real)

claim_a: The company was formed to acquire assets of a dissolved corporation, with an account dating from September 1, 1934
claim_b: The company was organized in August 1934; August 31, 1934 was 'the date of reorganization'
why_they_differ: Four printings of one company's own history, consistent at month level, none stating an incorporation act or a day.
best_supported_interpretation: Formation in August 1934 with accounting effect from September 1, 1934.
residual_uncertainty: The day, the state of incorporation, and whether this was a reincorporation or a purchase.
confidence: High (month) / Medium (the accounting start as an event)

claim_b: 'The twentieth anniversary of this subsidiary will occur July 22 of this year' - day-month, year by subtraction
why_they_differ: Two sentences in one company's own reports, eleven months apart, one giving a year and one giving a day-month with an implied year.
evidence_weight: Same lineage; the day-month is the only one of its kind in the corpus (sole July 22 and sole anniversary occurrence).
best_supported_interpretation: 1916-07-22 as the company's own anniversary belief, DERIVED, printed because shareholders could test it.
residual_uncertainty: What event July 22 marks; that the string 'July 22, 1916' never prints; the folk July 15 is unheld, not contradicted.

claim_a: Awarded under date of January 29, 1927 (two places)
claim_a_source: S4517 court's statement of facts and a brief
claim_b: Awarded 'on or about February 1, 1927'; contract entered 'on the 1st day of February, 1927'
claim_b_source: S4517 verified Bill paragraph 7 and Exhibit route-certificate recital
why_they_differ: A pleading's paraphrase of a departmental action versus the executed instrument's own date; the judicial summary gives a third.
evidence_weight: All three strings sit in ONE held volume - a within-carrier conflict, which adding another copy of the same record cannot resolve.
best_supported_interpretation: The instrument is dated February 1, 1927; the departmental award action is elsewhere stated as January 29, 1927.
residual_uncertainty: Which date a registry would record; whether 'on or about' conceals a third day.
confidence: High (that all three print) / Low (single true date)

claim_a: 'the lowest qualified bidder tendering sufficient guarantees'
why_they_differ: Two registers for the same statutory standard, one singular and one plural because the corporation and Hubbard were a pair.
best_supported_interpretation: The award rested on being lowest AND adequately guaranteed.
residual_uncertainty: Whether 'qualified' and 'responsible' were distinct tests; no held byte quotes the standard.

claim_b: Unfilled orders at December 31, 1940 were 196,522,446, 'an increase of 174,392,821 over unfilled orders at the close of the year 1939' - implying 22,129,625
why_they_differ: Scope: the 1940 figure is 'the Company's units in the United States'; the 1939 figure covers 'your Company and its subsidiaries' and includes approximately 900,000 CANADIAN dollars of Dominion work. The 872,949 gap is the same order of magnitude as that item, but the currencies differ.
evidence_weight: Both are the company's own printings of one register - one lineage; and 1940 also deconsolidated Canada.
best_supported_interpretation: Report both with their scope labels; do not average, do not restate 1939 onto a domestic basis.
residual_uncertainty: Whether the whole gap is the Canadian item and at what exchange basis.
confidence: High (both figures) / Low (any single reconciled number - none offered)

claim_a: Shares issued and outstanding 491,365 1/2 and still to be issued 30,517 3/4
claim_b: Those two sum to 521,883 1/4, not the printed total 521,883
why_they_differ: OCR destroys the fraction glyphs (halves as %, quarters as ^4).
evidence_weight: The FY1934 pair and the FY1940 pair both foot exactly, which localises the defect to this layer.
best_supported_interpretation: The 521,883 total stands; the 1935 split is unknown at the fraction.
residual_uncertainty: Which of the two figures carries the bad glyph. No third number substituted.

claim_a: FY1938 puts in quotation marks: 'the officers ... are convinced ... only by spending substantial sums in the development of new models'
claim_b: The held FY1934 text reads 'fairly substantial' and adds 'based upon their many years of experience' and 'in those fields which hold forth promise of producing future business'
why_they_differ: A within-lineage ellipsis-quotation that silently removes two hedges and upgrades the claim.
evidence_weight: Both documents are held on one shelf, so the discrepancy is MEASURED, not inferred. No outside source is involved.
best_supported_interpretation: Cite FY1934 for the hedged sentence; record FY1938 as a restatement with a strengthened claim.
residual_uncertainty: Whether other in-print quotations of earlier reports are also non-verbatim - only this pair is testable, because the FY1937 original is column-damaged.

claim_a: EDGAR's registrant header prints DATE OF NAME CHANGE 19730725 from BOEING AIRPLANE CO, in 26 of 33 held filings
claim_b: The renaming is generally placed in 1960 (dispatch brief's framing); no held byte supports 1960 and the FY1945 layer still prints Boeing Airplane Company
why_they_differ: One is a securities-registry field recording when the conformed name on the registrant's entry changed; the other is a corporate-history claim about a charter act.
evidence_weight: A is Tier-1 registry data re-printed mechanically - one record, 26 printings, NOT 26 corroborations. B is unheld.
best_supported_interpretation: The registrant's EDGAR conformed name changed on 1973-07-25; the corporate act and its date are UNKNOWN, bounded by held print to after FY1945 and no later than FY1976.
residual_uncertainty: The whole 1946-1976 range; the 39 unopened corporate-print layers would close it.
confidence: High (of the field's printing) / Low (as the act)

claim_a: The structural acts are explained by tax and administrative simplification and an industry trend - three printings, 1934, 1937, 1938
why_they_differ: 'antitrust' occurs 0 times adjacent to any Boeing naming in the 25 held text files (its single occurrence anywhere is in a volume where Boeing occurs 0 times); 'Sherman Act' 0; the only instruments the corpus prints are postal (the Act of April 29, 1930) and the February 9, 1934 annulment order.
evidence_weight: A stated motive printed three times by the issuer outranks nothing here, because the alternative motive is absent rather than contradicted.
best_supported_interpretation: Record the stated motive as the corpus's motive; record any antitrust motive as UNTRIED - a motive the corpus does not reach, not one it denies.
residual_uncertainty: Why United Aircraft & Transport Corporation was dissolved at all; the 1934 letter only describes, it does not cause.
confidence: High (of the null) / UNKNOWN (the real motive)

claim_a: Probe counts, case-insensitive over 12 files: Boeing Air Transport 145, Boeing Airplane Company 61, Boeing Aircraft Company 51
claim_b: This pass, case-sensitive exact phrase over 25 files: 89 / 43 / 61
why_they_differ: Case, file population, and whether substring noise is included.
evidence_weight: Both reproducible; neither is a naming census. Demonstrated noise in this very corpus: 403 of 497 William hits and 406 of 408 1917 hits sit in a volume with no Boeing; West 33/50 all resolve to addresses, case names, a carrier and a Weston; Green to a rival's secretary, an attorney general and a river; ATTA to hundreds of substring matches.
best_supported_interpretation: Publish only read-line namings with their entity adjacency quoted, and state the command and file population with every count.
residual_uncertainty: Whether a case-insensitive pass would surface a naming this one missed.

claim_a: First audited profit, 374,655.29, with deliveries exceeding the previous three years combined, and the accounting change having 'the desirable effect'
claim_b: The auditors state that the change made pre-tax income approximately 163,000 higher than the former policy, that Canada was excluded from consolidation for the first time, and that a further approximately 500,000 loss was expected on the option Clippers
claim_b_source: S4515 Note 1 and the Accountants' Report
why_they_differ: Not a disagreement about facts - a disagreement about framing, inside one document.
evidence_weight: Equal authority, because the auditors themselves wrote the number.
best_supported_interpretation: The first profit is 374,655.29 net, of which 163,000 pre-tax (28.9%) is attributable by the auditors to a policy change, on a basis that also deconsolidated Canada and still carried a (303,520.30) deficit.
residual_uncertainty: Whether the change was permitted, required or chosen; the auditors state it without endorsing it.

claim_a: A person of the founder's name is sworn in-window as President of Boeing Air Transport, Inc.
claim_a_source: S4517 oath and four signature blocks
claim_b: He appears in no board or officer list of any of the seven held corporate-print layers, including the 1940 proxy that names nine directors with share counts
why_they_differ: They describe different corporations; no held byte connects the roles.
evidence_weight: A is Tier-1 sworn; B is Tier-1 self-print; neither contradicts the other.
best_supported_interpretation: A founder-name officer is documented for one Boeing corporation in the air-mail record and is not documented for the reporting companies or their operating subsidiaries in 1934-40.
residual_uncertainty: His role, capital, shareholding, and departure - UNKNOWN; family (e) untried.

claim_a: The item holds one text layer per year, 1934-1978
claim_b: One of the two 1934 parts is an undated Hamilton Metalplane advertisement whose footer names a Milwaukee division of United Aircraft and Transport Corp.
why_they_differ: A FILE census is not a DOCUMENT census; the bound brochure is undated and internally inconsistent (H-45 heading over an H-15 table; eight seats in the table, six passengers in the text).
evidence_weight: The artefact is primary as an artefact and worthless as a dating witness.
best_supported_interpretation: Hold it as evidence that the name Boeing Airplane Company was used of a UATC division at Milwaukee, date UNKNOWN; count in-window reports as SIX, not seven.
residual_uncertainty: The brochure's year; who bound it with the reports.

claim_a: West, Green, C & F and Boeing are treated as namings
claim_b: Read in context they resolve to addresses, case captions, a rival carrier's secretary, a Wyoming attorney general and its replacement treasurer (Harry R. Weston), a river, and a Seattle board interlock at Pacific Car & Foundry Company
why_they_differ: Substring matching without entity adjacency manufactures a co-builder and a competitor out of street names and tax officials.
evidence_weight: Directly measured in the held bytes; C & F 0 occurrences, Montreal 0, Westhoff 0, Pacific Airplane 0, B & W 0.
best_supported_interpretation: Promote a naming only where the entity word is adjacent to a verb of being, acting or contracting, and after checking whether the naming refers to Wichita, Seattle or Vancouver.
residual_uncertainty: The FY1940 proxy prints FAUL PIGOTT while the same file's board page prints PAUL PIGOTT; both are recorded as printed.

claim_a: Boeing Company (64 occurrences) and The Boeing Company (25) appear in held bytes, apparently dating the modern name into the window
claim_b: In the 1933 volume 'Boeing Company' is a DEFINED TERM of a municipal airport lease for the Washington-authorized carrier, and the out-of-window hits are 1970s NASA divisions; the volume itself is a Wyoming gasoline-tax suit, not an air-mail case
why_they_differ: A contract's shorthand and a digitiser's anachronism.
evidence_weight: The lease and the testimony are Tier-1 record; the name form is not a corporate-naming event.
best_supported_interpretation: Cite the Edelman volume for (i) a third-party federal officer's testimony of mail handling and (ii) a municipal lease describing an 'airplane line extending from Chicago ... to San Francisco' - never for the registrant's origin.
residual_uncertainty: The Supreme Court disposition of the tax case is unprinted.

claim_a: 'a termination by Boeing of its contract with Transcontinental & Western Air, Inc.'
claim_b: T.W.A. 'likewise contended that the contract was terminated and that it intended to claim damages'
why_they_differ: Both parties asserted termination; the only account is the party that kept the 397,500 down payment.
evidence_weight: One audited-adjacent self-report; no counter-party document and no docket is held.
best_supported_interpretation: The bytes establish a dispute and a retained deposit, not a breacher.
residual_uncertainty: Settlement terms; whether the five T.W.A. Stratoliners in the 1939 backlog are that settlement - plausible, unproven, never joined in a sentence by the documents.
